title: South Korean cross-country sprint pair disqualified for use of eco-unfriendly wax
content:
A pair of South Korean cross-country skiers were disqualified from Tuesday’s women’s sprint event after being caught using a banned substance, fluor, as part of their ski wax.

Han Dasom and Lee Eui-jin had both taken part in the qualification time trial, where neither advanced to the knockout races, but were subsequently disqualified from the results by the FIS after a routine kit examination.

Fluor was banned from competition in 2023 due to its lack of biodegradable properties, with scientific studies demonstrating its polluting effect on melted snow run-off. The FIS has also classified it as a risk to human health due to the body’s inability to break it down, previously stating that use of the compound placed wax-technicians at risk.

Cross-country skiers will typically use bespoke ski wax combinations to improve performance on specific conditions — the snow at the Tesero Cross Country Stadium has proved challenging all week due to its humidity.

Initially adapted from use on sailing boats, where it improved their gliding ability, the FIS have described how fluor’s water-repellent qualities are “a big advantage in wet or humid conditions”.

Speaking to South Korean news agency Newsis, a representative of the Korea Ski Association denied purposeful wrongdoing.

“The athletes’ products are not fluorine wax,” they said. “They tested negative in all previous international competitions with no prior issues. We are also perplexed.

“We will consult experts from wax and ski manufacturers to investigate whether the issue lies with the wax or skis.”

This is the second incident involving fluor at these Olympics, with Japanese snowboarder Shiba Masaki disqualified from men’s parallel giant slalom qualification on Monday.
